Report_ID: Five times sit-to-stand test (5STS) completion time at 6 months
Title: Exercise in Patients on Dialysis: A Multicenter, Randomized Clinical Trial
Author: Manfredini et al.
Comment: The paper reports 104 exercise and 123 control participants as having repeated the 6-month evaluations overall, but it also states that at 6 months 4 exercise and 7 control participants could not perform any repetition and 9 exercise and 15 control participants could not complete the 5STS. Because the exact per-arm N underlying the reported endpoint completion-time means and SDs is not explicitly stated, group Ns are left null rather than inferred. M_diff follows the extraction schema definition group_2 minus group_1 (= control minus exercise, +2.0 seconds); the synthesis-requested exercise-minus-control contrast is therefore -2.0 seconds.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Walking exercise / active arm') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Design Type: Multicenter open-label parallel two-group randomized controlled trial
Study Environment: Home-based exercise on nondialysis days; assessments at participating nephrology units on nondialysis days
Medium: Home-based walking exercise guided by a metronome and managed/encouraged by dialysis staff
interaction_type: Dialysis-staff-managed home exercise with rehabilitation-team oversight
Participant type: Adults with stage G5 CKD receiving maintenance haemodialysis or continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis
Recruitment source: Patients from 13 participating Nephrology Units; randomized patients were enrolled in nine centers
Outcome measurement: Time to complete five sit-to-stand repetitions at the 6-month end-of-intervention assessment
Outcome variable: Five times sit-to-stand test (5STS) completion time at 6 months
effect_direction: Exercise minus control; negative values indicate shorter completion time and favor exercise.

Title: Effect of individualized exercise during maintenance haemodialysis on exercise capacity and health-related quality of life in patients with uraemia
Author: Wu et al.
Comment: The table lists the exercise group first, so M_diff follows the extraction-field rule group_2 minus group_1: control minus exercise = 3.7 s. For the synthesis-requested orientation exercise minus control, reverse the sign to -3.7 s (favours exercise). SE_diff was computed from the explicitly reported endpoint SDs and analysed group sizes as sqrt(6.8^2/32 + 7.2^2/33). The paper reports only P < 0.05 for this comparison, not an exact p-value or t statistic, so those fields are null.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Test group: individualized recumbent cycling during haemodialysis') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Study Environment: Intradialytic intervention at Beilun People’s Hospital, Ningbo
Medium: Individualized recumbent stationary cycling during haemodialysis
Topic of Content: Exercise capacity and lower-limb functional strength
Recruitment source: Outpatients receiving long-term maintenance haemodialysis at Beilun People’s Hospital
follow_up_timepoint: End of intervention at approximately 3 months
effect_direction: Exercise minus control; negative values indicate shorter completion time and favor exercise.

Title: Effects of Resistance Exercise Training and Nandrolone Decanoate on Body Composition and Muscle Function among Patients Who Receive Hemodialysis: A Randomized, Controlled Trial
Author: Johansen et al.
Comment: The synthesis requires pooled endpoint mean, SD, and analyzed n for exercise versus no exercise. This factorial trial reports four cell-specific endpoint means/SDs and an exercise main-effect P value, but no outcome-specific analyzed n by cell or marginal exercise groups. Therefore pooled exercise/no-exercise means, SDs, Ns, MD, and SE were left null rather than using randomized Ns or inventing endpoint Ns. The reported ± values in Tables 2 and 4 are treated as SDs based on the table presentation and Table 1's explicit mean ± SD convention, but no cell values are entered because the requested row is the factorial exercise contrast.; ANOVA excluded: comparison_type='mixed' is not between-group
Design Type: Randomized 2 × 2 factorial controlled trial with repeated measures
Study Environment: University of California, San Francisco–affiliated outpatient dialysis units; exercise performed during hemodialysis
Medium: Supervised lower-extremity resistance exercise using ankle weights during hemodialysis
Topic of Content: Lower-extremity muscle strengthening and physical performance
Recruitment source: University of California, San Francisco–affiliated outpatient dialysis units
Outcome measurement: Time to rise from a chair five times, assessed on a day after dialysis at baseline and 3 months
additional_group_ns: Randomized arm sizes reported elsewhere: Placebo n=20; ND n=19; EX n=20; ND+EX n=20. These are not used as endpoint analyzed Ns because the paper states that 68 completed and does not report outcome-specific analyzed Ns.
follow_up_timepoint: End of intervention at approximately 3 months
effect_direction: Exercise minus control; negative values indicate shorter completion time and favor exercise.

Title: The Effect of Interdialytic Combined Resistance and Aerobic Exercise Training on Health Related Outcomes in Chronic Hemodialysis Patients: The Tunisian Randomized Controlled Study
Author: Frih et al.
Comment: Table 2's transcribed header is misaligned; values were mapped in the stated table order as control initial 31.7 ± 2.5, control final 32 ± 3.1, intervention initial 32 ± 3.5, and intervention final 27 ± 2.9. M_diff was computed from the explicit final means as intervention minus control: 27 - 32 = -5 s. The paper reports P < 0.001 rather than an exact p value, so p_value is null. Degrees of freedom for the STS-10 F statistic are not explicitly printed and were left null.
Design Type: Single-blinded randomized controlled trial with baseline and final repeated assessments
Study Environment: Interdialytic exercise on non-hemodialysis days; CHU Monastir
Medium: Supervised in-person combined resistance and aerobic exercise
Content length: 4 months; 64 sessions; four approximately 60-minute sessions per week
Topic of Content: Lower-limb functional strength and physical capacity
Participant type: Male adults receiving chronic maintenance haemodialysis
Recruitment source: Nephrology and Internal Medicine Service of CHU Monastir
Outcome measurement: Final assessment immediately after the four-month intervention; time required to complete 10 consecutive sit-to-stand-to-sit repetitions
effect_direction: Exercise minus control; negative values indicate shorter completion time and favor exercise.

Title: Effects of exercise training on aerobic and functional capacity of end-stage renal disease patients
Author: Koufaki, Mercer and Naish
Comment: Endpoint values (not change scores) were extracted. Table 6 gives outcome-specific analyzed samples ET n=14 and C n=13, smaller than the overall completer samples. M_diff follows the extraction schema convention group 2 minus group 1 (control minus exercise = 1.7 s); for the requested synthesis direction, exercise minus control, reverse the sign to obtain -1.7 s. The reported F=10.4 and P=0.003 refer to the repeated-measures time-by-group interaction, not the unadjusted endpoint contrast; degrees of freedom were not stated.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Exercise training group (ET)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)

domain: Exercise rehabilitation in end-stage renal disease/maintenance dialysis
Study Environment: CAPD patients trained in the Renal Rehabilitation Gym; haemodialysis patients trained during the first 2 hours of dialysis
Topic of Content: Aerobic and functional capacity in maintenance dialysis patients

Recruitment source: Patients undergoing CAPD or haemodialysis; specific recruitment site/source not explicitly stated

Title: A single-blind randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effect of 6 months of progressive aerobic exercise training in patients with uraemic restless legs syndrome
Author: Christoforos D. Giannaki et al.
Comment: M_diff was computed from the explicitly reported endpoint means (exercise minus control: 8.5 − 8.5 = 0.0) for this simple two-group trial. The Table 3 row labels STS-5 as “(repetitions)” rather than explicitly stating seconds, although Methods/footnote identify it as the five-repetition sit-to-stand test; therefore outcome_units was left null rather than inferred. P=0.003 is the exercise arm’s within-group baseline-to-post comparison and was not entered as the endpoint treatment-versus-control P value. The reported between-group change-score comparison was P=0.045, but the requested endpoint values were extracted instead.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Progressive exercise training group') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Single-blind, two-arm parallel randomized controlled trial
domain: Haemodialysis exercise training and functional capacity
Study Environment: Intradialytic exercise at the haemodialysis units of the University Hospital of Larisa and General Hospital of Trikala
Content length: 45 minutes three times per week for 6 months
Topic of Content: Progressive aerobic cycling exercise versus no-resistance sham cycling
Participant type: Patients with uraemic restless legs syndrome receiving maintenance haemodialysis
Recruitment source: Haemodialysis units of the University Hospital of Larisa and the General Hospital of Trikala

Report_ID: End-of-intervention Sit to Stand test completion time (10 repetitions)
Title: The Efects of Aquatic Exercise on Functional Capacity and Health-Related Quality of Life in Hemodialysis Patients
Author: Anastasia et al.
Comment: The paper lists the exercise arm first. Per the extraction convention, M_diff is group 2 minus group 1 = control minus exercise = 21.2 - 15.2 = 6.0 seconds. For the synthesis-requested orientation (exercise minus control), the raw MD is -6.0 seconds. The assessment is labeled 'Follow up' in Table 2 but is explicitly the end of the four-month training programme, not a later post-programme follow-up. The test used 10 repetitions, which is eligible under the specified five-to-ten-repetition rule.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Group A: therapeutic aquatic exercise program') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Two-arm parallel randomized controlled trial with baseline and 4-month repeated assessments
Study Environment: Supervised swimming-pool exercise on non-dialysis days
Content length: Four-month program; three 60-minute sessions per week
Topic of Content: Therapeutic aquatic exercise for haemodialysis patients
Participant type: Patients with chronic kidney disease receiving maintenance haemodialysis
Outcome measurement: Time required to perform 10 consecutive sit-to-stand repetitions as fast as possible, assessed at the end of the four-month programme
Outcome variable: End-of-intervention Sit to Stand test completion time (10 repetitions)
effect_direction: Exercise minus control; negative values indicate shorter completion time and favor exercise.
